name: What is the difference between double-pane and triple-pane energy-efficient windows?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between double-pane and triple-pane energy-efficient windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in the number of glass panes and the insulation they provide. Double-pane windows have two layers of glass with an inert gas like argon or krypton sealed between them, offering good insulation. Triple-pane windows add a third layer of glass and another gas-filled space, providing superior thermal performance and noise reduction. While triple-pane windows offer better energy efficiency and soundproofing, they are typically heavier and more expensive. Double-pane windows are often a cost-effective choice for many climates, including Southern California, balancing performance with affordability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Double-pane has two glass layers with gas fill; triple-pane adds a third layer for superior insulation and noise reduction but is heavier and more costly.
